import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source3_93_0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_93/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source3_93_1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_93/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source3_93_2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_93/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source3_93_1 and Source3_93_2 on "movie_id"
joined_df = pd.merge(source3_93_1, source3_93_2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Operation 2: GROUP BY Source3_93_1.movie_id and aggregate count(Source3_93_1.user_id)
# Since after join, movie_id is from Source3_93_1 (same column), group by 'movie_id' and count 'user_id'
grouped = joined_df.groupby("movie_id", as_index=False).agg({ "user_id": "count" })

# Rename columns to match target schema: ['movie_id': integer, '0': integer]
grouped.rename(columns={"user_id": "0"}, inplace=True)

# Ensure data types match target schema
grouped["movie_id"] = grouped["movie_id"].astype(int)
grouped["0"] = grouped["0"].astype(int)

# Write the result to the target CSV file
grouped.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_93/target_multisource.csv", index=False)
